execution.note: All 12 cells passed their evidence checks. Censoring was recorded and analyzed as per-trial lower bounds; no cell was dropped or retried.

identity.reason: Same workload settings as multiwindow-10k-8192, but a different stop rule and analysis: censoring is recorded as per-trial lower bounds instead of aborting the experiment. The first C=1 cell is reused from the stopped plan because its settings are identical; the remaining 11 cells are new.

methodology.problem: The 2048, 8192, and 16384 pilots all show a reasoning-only ceiling tail. Zero censoring in 240 trials is not a feasible design at a 5% rate, so the zero-censoring stop rule blocks the benchmark rather than protecting it.
methodology.bounded_analysis: A ceiling-truncated trial contributes its cap-hit time as a per-trial lower bound on completion latency. Every order statistic of the lower bounds is a lower bound on the corresponding order statistic of the true completion times. A lower bound above an upper-bound threshold proves failure; a lower bound below it stays inconclusive. No threshold is ratified, so the analysis is descriptive.
methodology.implementation: src/endpoint_bench/bounds.py, tested by tests/test_bounds.py; scripts/analyze_bounded.py pools the 12 cells.
methodology.outside_contract: The 1.1 contract's dq.truncation_rate gate still treats any censoring as invalid. This experiment is outside that gate and outside the 1024-token contract scope. It produces bounded descriptive evidence, not a contract verdict.

authorization.authorized_by: Owner session goal: "Complete all performance benchmarks"
authorization.scope: The remaining 11 cells of a six-window, two-cell 10K experiment at an 8192-token ceiling, plus the reused C=1 cell from run-6cabf9e5ee70-w1-c1. Censoring is allowed and analyzed as lower bounds.
authorization.note: This authorization covers only this bounded experiment. It does not authorize a higher ceiling, a different deployment, a contract verdict, or a qualification claim.

design.interleaving: Odd windows run C=1 first, even windows run C=2 first. Window 1's C=1 cell is the reused run; its C=2 cell and windows 2-6 are new.
design.wall_time_basis: The 8192 pilot took 58 s and the censored cell 87 s. Ten-minute offsets leave room for provider variance; if a pair overruns the next offset, stop and revise rather than overlap.

cost.note: Client-side conservative bound assuming every request reaches the 8192 cap. Actual spend is expected to be far lower. Not a provider billing limit.

stop_rules.criterion: Censoring is not a stop condition. It is recorded and analyzed as a lower bound. The experiment stops only when the evidence itself is invalid.
stop_sequence_on: a harness failure, nonzero engine exit without parseable evidence, or process timeout
planned requests not equal to actual HTTP attempts
a provider-versus-target conformance failure outside the profile tolerance
missing validated engine schema or raw evidence
a cell overrunning the next window offset
stop_rules.on_failure: Stop the sequence, preserve artifacts, and do not retry, replace trials, raise the ceiling, or merge cells with different settings. Review and version a new plan.
prohibited: raising the output ceiling to reduce censoring
dropping censored trials from the pooled sample
claiming a completion-latency mean or percentile as exact rather than bounded
merging this experiment with the stopped plan's uncensored interpretation

analysis.pooling: Pool per-trial lower bounds at each concurrency level across all six windows. Publish per-window counts beside the pooled bounds.
analysis.estimator: linear_interpolation_of_closest_ranks for p50/p95; arithmetic mean for mean
analysis.censoring_rule: Never drop a censored trial. Never compute a natural-completion-only mean or percentile and present it as the sample's latency.
analysis.interpretation: The pooled p50/p95 are lower bounds. They can prove an upper-bound objective is missed; they cannot prove one is met. Thresholds remain null.

qualification.note: Outside the 1.1 contract's 1024-token scope and zero-censoring gate. No verdict is produced and no endpoint is qualified.
